svg.text: Rule 30 damage cone from one extra live cell
The left panel is the ordinary one-cell seed. The right panel is the XOR difference after adding one extra live cell nearby.
Rule 30 does not just spread activity. It amplifies a tiny local perturbation into a wide irregular cone that keeps shedding structure row after row.
Single live cell at the center. The familiar wedge appears immediately, but it stays internally jagged.
Damage cone after one adjacent flip
XOR difference between the base run and a run with one extra live cell offset by +3 at step 0.
How much of each row is changed?
The difference never settles into a smooth ramp. The changed share keeps breathing as the cone roughens.
How wide is the damaged region?
By step 117 the difference span already covers more than 95% of the row width in this bounded run.
Generated by c/rule30_damage_cone_svg.c with width 241, 120 steps, and a +3-cell perturbation.
